consumer: The engine's NPC trade interface (trade dialogue/menu loop) that the player drives to give some items and take others, asking 'did this give/take exchange actually settle through the trade mechanism?'
scope: The interactive two-sided trade transaction: select offers from BOTH the avatar's and the shopkeeper's inventories, the value balance, and the confirm/cancel step driven through the real active input loop
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_carried_items — it only serializes the avatar's wielded/worn/inventory items as a static read-only array; it never invokes the trade prompt, sees the NPC's side, or moves any item
divergence: Player offers a knife to the shopkeeper and takes a canteen in return: the carried_items dump reflects a static inventory read and cannot exercise the offer/confirm menu, so a completed trade vs a shopkeeper refusal (unfavorable value balance) are indistinguishable and the NPC's side of the exchange is entirely invisible
